institutionName: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A good university and a smaller city

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. They help us a lot at NTNU

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They gave folders and check list for all international students

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was okay to find. I used the Norwegian site
Hyble.no
and found housing through there. It was very well organized

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: if you would like to live more quite by yourself it can be beneficial to try and find housing outside campus

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: as a danish student in Norway is was very easy, I should just confirm my arrival

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was always people from the university to help you

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was a little harder because the classes I wanted wasn't offered when I arrived, so I had to find other interesting courses. But you were welcome to try some out for a period before committing which was nice

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont stress about it before arriving, you have good time to decide

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses were very good and interesting, it was just a little ashame that my education was not that well represented

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 3 BA courses and 1 MA course. It was mainly because it was outside of my field. but many of the courses were highly relevant and had a high level

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very much the same style. I would wish for more student participation in NTNU

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Norway 
Gender And Norwegian Culture
Innovation in Global Health 
Enviornmental Politics and Ressource management

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked Enviornmental Politics and Ressource management because it was very relevant and showed many different nuances on climate change and environmental problems. The teacher was very talented and motivated.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I think i expected all the costs. Norway is a expensive country.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Gym membership and transportation for students were quite cheap

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a large sports enviornment were you could join any club you wanted from volleyball, poledance to horseback riding, and handball

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: be a part of the SIT gyms and try out fun classes. Or be a part of the NTNUI were you could rent cabins really cheap and go on hike and cabin trips and explore the Norwegian nature

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking around the area. And if you are there in the winter go crosscountry skiing

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy since Norway and Danmark are very similar

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a voulenteer club. that is the way in to get to know norwegians, but there are many social event for exchange students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The Norwegian people are a little closed off and can be difficult to approach. They are very sweet when you talk to them, but they dont seem that interested in being friends.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their love for nature

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. try and go to the social events in the beginning to meet new people 
2. try out a sport you never tried before 
3. Dont stress about courses, there are plenty of time to find what works

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember that shops are closed on sundays

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting sweet people

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The Norwegian dark winter

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
